falsifier.proves_red: DONE when, in an isolated instance: (1) a component whose source changed reads red from the first inspector pass with no human act; (2) a repair that leaves the proof file's hash unchanged reseals green through the door; (3) a reseal whose proof hash differs is REFUSED without a ruling id and ACCEPTED with one, and the refusal names the hash it saw; (4) a red left unrepaired lands exactly one trouble in the operator inbox carrying the stderr tail, and that trouble clears on the next pass after a green reseal; (5) the door is reachable only from the pre-commit hook and a direct call — grep finds no caller on any pulse path. WRONG INTENT if the door ever writes a seal for a proof it did not just run, or if any rung restores green without a run.

questions.a: Two named. (1) The proof file's hash bounds 'the proof's assertions' — load-bearing and only true once the seal fingerprint covers the proof's import closure (idea 7bdf2d19671d); recorded as a dependency, the idea's own order. (2) Pre-commit over staged files is the only firing event needed — standing, because an uncommitted change is not yet the machine's state; the residue (a never-committed drift) is named, not hidden.

One point asserted wrapped was not: who is 'the competent agent' in code. Wrapped as: nobody — the door does not identify the repairer; it bounds the repair (hash) and records who fired it (the existing caller field on run_proof). Codemother becomes a repairer when she has a hand; the door does not change for that.

Consulted the lab. Ruling 2026-09-06 (the ladder) — this is its physics. CLAUDE.md IOU 'deterministic red is fixed or carries a ruling' — same why, this narrows it to two admitted dispositions for seals. Corrosion's constraint_set — not a collision; a seal door that narrowed would fire its self-reference tooth, which is the desired coupling. Ideas 5dcad5c80d6e (this), 7bdf2d19671d (fingerprint, dependency) and fb5d259e4396 (bind-not-copy, a cost fix the door benefits from) are siblings from one conversation; recorded on the ticket.

A Haiku-level builder needs: (a) where — cairn/devices/tester/reseal_door.py (new) using run_proof from device.py and the store in validation_store.py; (b) the red record — on a red run, write `<component>/validations/<proof>.red.json` with proof_hash (sha256 of the proof file), stderr tail (last 40 lines), when, caller; (c) the reseal rule — accept when sha256(proof) == red.proof_hash, or when the packet carries `ruling_id` that resolves under CairnCommons/decisions/ and is confirmed; refuse otherwise, printing both hashes; (d) the trouble — identity `seal-red-<component>` via trouble.raise_trouble, cleared by the same door on green; (e) the hook — `.git/hooks/pre-commit` calls `python3 -m cairn.devices.tester.reseal_door --staged`, replicated by the launcher's hook install; (f) don't — no call from any on_pulse, no seal without a run, no reading of the proof's assertions (the hash IS the bound). All written into the ticket's how.

constraints: Red at measurement, and red through every rung until reproven — design never restores green.
Two dispositions for a deterministic red: fixed (proof hash unchanged) or a confirmed ruling id in the same act. No third.
Fired from pre-commit over staged files; never from any on_pulse path.
how: The tester gains a reseal door (the idea): census standing seals, rerun every proof whose source_fingerprint no longer matches, land the new seals. Rung 1 is already physics — component_color in build_inspector reds on mismatch and raises inspector-new-finding troubles — so the door reuses it and adds the three missing rungs. Rung 2, BOUNDED REPAIR: the door reruns the proof; if it is red, the competent agent (CC or Akien today) may change anything that leaves the proof's assertions byte-identical — the door records the proof file's hash at red and refuses a reseal whose proof hash differs unless a ruling id sits in the same act. Rung 3, TROUBLE: a red that is not repaired within the session lands in the operator inbox with the stderr tail, as one trouble per component (the existing identity scheme), and self-clears on the next pass once the seal matches. Rung 4, DESIGN: 'the proof's claim no longer matches the spec' is a ruling, opened by Akien through `cairn ruling open`; the door accepts a reseal with a changed proof only with that ruling's id, and the component stays red until reproven under it. Greens finish silently. Fired from a git pre-commit hook over the staged files, never from the beat.

challenge.better_approach: Letting component_color alone stand (rung 1 only, today's state) leaves the repair unbounded and unrecorded — the plaster reflex has no wall. A nightly cron audit was the shape CC first asked about; Akien's ladder is event-shaped ('not an alarm'), and the idea already chose pre-commit over the beat so it never becomes a poller. Bounding repair by proof-file hash is the smallest wall that makes 'fix, or ruling' two dispositions and no third.
challenge.prior_art: component_color + _source_fingerprint in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py (rung 1, shipped); inspector-new-finding-* trouble identities and their self-clear (same file, ~3174); trouble.raise_trouble/clear in cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py; run_proof and the validation store in cairn/devices/tester/ (device.py, validation_store.py, isolation.py); the ruling door's own 'conformer must change AFTER intake' hash check (cairn ruling verify) is the exact pattern for 'proof hash unchanged since red'. The reseal idea 2026-09-06-a-reseal-door-on-the-tester-it is the origin and already lists the order (import-closure fingerprint first).
challenge.hidden_assumption: That 'the proof's assertions' can be bounded by the proof FILE's hash. A repair to a fixture the proof imports would change what is asserted without touching the file — that is the import-closure fingerprint (idea 7bdf2d19671d) and the ticket depends on it landing first, as the idea's own order says. Also assumes the pre-commit hook is the only event needed; a source change never committed leaves the seal expired but un-audited — acceptable, since an uncommitted change is not yet the machine's state (CLAUDE.md: the repo is the state).
challenge.real_collision: None. The 'deterministic red carries a ruling' IOU in CLAUDE.md has the same why and this is its physics for seals; the corrosion constraint_set already fires the self-reference tooth on narrowing. The tester's gated_by now co-lists codemother (35a915b): this door is exactly the kind of care-of-the-code process she owns, so the ticket homes under the tester with codemother as owner.

why_beneath_the_why: Akien 2026-09-06: 'if it cannot be reproven, that means something is no longer functioning correctly' — and a peer leans on a green it did not check (Law 8), so the moment a green stops being reproducible it has to stop being green without anyone having to notice.
